author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Altera said Tuesday that its parent company confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed public offering of common stock.

The programmable-chip company did not disclose how many shares could be offered or a potential price range. It said any offering remains subject to completion of the SEC review process, market conditions and other factors.

The filing is a concrete step beyond the company’s previously reported IPO preparations, but it does not guarantee that a listing will proceed on a particular timetable. Because the submission is confidential, the draft registration statement is not yet available for public review.

Altera describes itself as a provider of programmable computing and connectivity products used in data centers, communications networks, industrial equipment and AI-enabled systems. Intel sold a majority stake in the business to Silver Lake in 2025 while retaining a minority interest.
dek: The Silver Lake- and Intel-backed chipmaker says its parent submitted a draft Form S-1, while the potential offering’s size and price remain undetermined.
headline: Altera confidentially files for a U.S. initial public offering
